tables.name: financial_year
tables.description: Australian financial years covered (1 July to 30 June).
why: Every price, rule and window is tied to a year AND to explicit dates, so mid-year changes fit without breaking the yearly grain.

tables.name: distributor
tables.description: The 14 electricity distribution network service providers (DNSPs).
why: Time zone and DST live here because TOU windows are stated in local or standard time and QLD/NT have no daylight saving.

columns.name: name
columns.description: canonical name used by the reconciliation (scripts/schema.py CANON)

columns.name: iana_timezone
columns.description: IANA zone of the network area, e.g. Australia/Sydney

columns.name: observes_dst
columns.description: 1 when local clocks move for daylight saving

tables.name: document_series
tables.description: A publication that is reissued in versions (e.g. the AER 2025-26 consolidated stakeholder report v1..v5, or one distributor's price list for a year).
why: Versions of the same publication are grouped so 'latest version' and 'v1 vs approved' are simple queries; no version ever overwrites another.

tables.name: source_document
tables.description: One version of one document: the unit of provenance. Every value row points here.
why: Proposed, approved, AER and distributor numbers coexist because each is keyed by its own document version.
sha256 + URL + retrieval date make each file re-fetchable and tamper-evident.
Versions known to exist but not retrievable (AER login-gated files) are still recorded so the history has no silent gaps.
checks: retrieval_status <> 'retrieved' OR (local_path IS NOT NULL AND sha256 IS NOT NULL)

columns.name: document_id
columns.description: slug derived from the file name

columns.name: version_label
columns.description: as published, e.g. v1, v5, v1.1, 'updated 17 Jul 2024'

columns.name: price_status
columns.description: regulatory status of the prices in this version (mixed: differs by distributor, see document_coverage)

columns.name: recon_side
columns.description: role in the reconciliation: AER = AER-authored, AER_HOSTED = distributor document hosted on aer.gov.au, DNSP = distributor's own site

columns.name: publication_date
columns.description: date the version was published, when known

columns.name: source_url
columns.description: exact URL the file was retrieved from (or the landing page when not retrievable)

columns.name: retrieved_on
columns.description: date the file was retrieved (or the Wayback capture date)

columns.name: committed_in_repo
columns.description: 1 when the file itself is committed (Wayback copies)

tables.name: document_coverage
tables.description: Which distributors' prices an AER consolidated version carries, and whether they are proposed or approved there (from the AER changelog).
why: One AER file mixes proposed and approved prices by jurisdiction (2025-26 v3: approved ACT/NSW/TAS/VIC, proposed QLD/SA/NT), so price status is per (document, distributor), not per document.
Versions the AER no longer serves are still covered, so the history of what was published when is complete even where the file is gone.

columns.name: price_status
columns.description: status of that distributor's prices in that version

columns.name: evidence_document_id
columns.description: saved AER landing page holding the changelog

columns.name: locator
columns.description: Where in the document: xlsx:<sheet>!<cell>, pdf:p<page>, pdf-ocr:p<page> or html:text (grammar in scripts/tariffdb/locators.py)

columns.name: quote
columns.description: Verbatim wording from the document at the locator (whitespace-insensitive match is tested)

tables.name: document_ingestion
tables.description: Explicit extraction coverage for every held or unavailable source document.
why: A source inventory entry is not evidence that its prices were extracted; independent row counts expose empty or rules-only documents.
checks: charge_count >= 0 AND listing_count >= 0 AND eligibility_count >= 0 AND tou_schedule_count >= 0 AND metering_count >= 0

columns.name: charge_count
columns.description: Number of charge rows read from this source

columns.name: eligibility_count
columns.description: Structured or quoted requirements from this source

tables.name: tariff
tables.description: Stable identity of a network tariff across years: the distributor's own code.
why: Codes are the only identifier both sides share; names and labels drift every year.
Codes the AER prints that no distributor document uses stay as their own identity (identity_basis) instead of being force-matched.

columns.name: identity_basis
columns.description: where the canonical code comes from

tables.name: tariff_alias
tables.description: Other labels under which a tariff is published: AER code labels, AER tariff IDs, joint labels ('010, 011*'), regional suffixes.
why: Code-label quirks are data, not code: each alias is tied to the document it appears in.

tables.name: tariff_relation
tables.description: Relationships between tariffs: renames, replacements, opt-out alternatives, export companions.
why: Renames across years (e.g. SAPN RELE -> RESELE) keep both identities and link them, so history is never rewritten.

columns.name: fin_year
columns.description: year the relation is stated for

columns.name: locator
columns.description: Where in the document: xlsx:<sheet>!<cell>, pdf:p<page>, pdf-ocr:p<page> or html:text (grammar in scripts/tariffdb/locators.py)

columns.name: quote
columns.description: Verbatim wording from the document at the locator (whitespace-insensitive match is tested)

tables.name: tariff_listing
tables.description: A tariff as listed in one document version (code, name and class as printed there).
why: The historical grain: one row per (document version, tariff); attributes are never updated, a new version adds a new listing.
is_priced = 0 represents AER zero-priced placeholder rows without inventing charges.

columns.name: code_published
columns.description: code exactly as printed (joint, starred ...); NULL when the row prints no code (AER 2025-26 v1)

columns.name: class_published
columns.description: tariff class / customer class heading as printed

columns.name: region
columns.description: pricing region or zone when the document splits one code by region

columns.name: effective_from
columns.description: first day the listed prices apply

columns.name: price_availability
columns.description: Whether this document prints prices, a zero/blank placeholder, or only rules

columns.name: is_priced
columns.description: 0 when the source has no priced components (placeholder); explicit zero charges remain prices

columns.name: locator
columns.description: first price cell/page of the listing

tables.name: listing_flag
tables.description: Status flags of a listing: trial, closed to new customers, withdrawn, site-specific, placeholder, proposed price, LFiT/metering inclusion.
why: A tariff can be several of these at once and they change by year, so they are rows, not columns.

tables.name: charge
tables.description: One published price component of one listing in one price basis (NUoS/DUoS/TUoS/...).
why: Value and unit are kept exactly as published (value_published, unit_published, value_raw) next to the normalised value (value_std in cents; fixed charges per day; demand per billing period).
Inclusion of metering and LFiT is explicit per row because AER and distributor totals differ by them.
Every row carries a locator that the tests re-read from the source file.
checks: (locator_kind = 'xlsx' AND sheet IS NOT NULL AND cell IS NOT NULL AND page IS NULL) OR (locator_kind <> 'xlsx' AND page IS NOT NULL AND sheet IS NULL AND cell IS NULL)

columns.name: price_basis
columns.description: NUoS = total network price; DUoS/TUoS/DPPC/JSA components; metering

columns.name: component_label
columns.description: component label as published (header hierarchy joined with ' - ')

columns.name: season
columns.description: normalised season (summer, non_summer, high, low, winter)

columns.name: value_published
columns.description: number exactly as displayed in the document

columns.name: unit_interpreted
columns.description: Unit used for conversion; differs only where the source parser supplies a period or repairs a source typo

columns.name: normalisation_note
columns.description: Reason the conversion unit differs from the printed unit

columns.name: value_raw
columns.description: full-precision cell value for spreadsheets (NULL for PDFs)

columns.name: unit_std
columns.description: c/day, c/kWh, c/kVAh, c/kW/<period>, c/kVA/<period>, c/lamp/day ...

columns.name: period_inferred
columns.description: 1 when the period comes from the component label, not the published unit

columns.name: includes_metering
columns.description: whether the value contains a metering charge

columns.name: includes_lfit
columns.description: whether the value contains the ACT large-scale feed-in tariff amount

columns.name: locator
columns.description: where the value is (re-read by the tests)

tables.name: charge_step
tables.description: Quantity blocks or export allowances, separate from tariff eligibility thresholds.
why: Consumption blocks reset independently of eligibility: a 60 kWh/day block is not a customer assignment threshold.
Open-ended upper bounds use NULL; inclusivity and reset period prevent ambiguous boundaries.
checks: lower_bound IS NULL OR upper_bound IS NULL OR lower_bound < upper_bound

columns.name: step_group
columns.description: The quantity divided into blocks, as the source names it (e.g. 'Anytime Energy'); the blocks of one (tariff, document, step_group) form one ladder

columns.name: upper_bound
columns.description: Upper quantity boundary, NULL means unbounded

columns.name: lower_inclusive
columns.description: Whether lower boundary belongs to the block

columns.name: upper_inclusive
columns.description: Whether upper boundary belongs to the block

columns.name: locator
columns.description: Where in the document: xlsx:<sheet>!<cell>, pdf:p<page>, pdf-ocr:p<page> or html:text (grammar in scripts/tariffdb/locators.py)

columns.name: quote
columns.description: Verbatim wording from the document at the locator (whitespace-insensitive match is tested)

tables.name: metering_price
tables.description: Metering prices: the AER Metering worksheet (2025-26 on), the AER 2024-25 'Tariff schedule 1', and the per-tariff Metering block of the Energex/Ergon price lists.
why: The AER prints network prices without metering and metering separately; storing both lets the distributor's metering-inclusive daily charge be reproduced exactly ($/yr x 100 / 365).
charge_basis keeps 'per year' vs exit fee vs unstated apart: the sheet mixes them in one column.

columns.name: tariff_codes_published
columns.description: content of the sheet's 'Tariff code' column as printed (tariff codes, or metering-service codes such as MP7)

columns.name: tariff_id
columns.description: tariff the row belongs to (per-tariff blocks only)

columns.name: component_label
columns.description: price component the block value adds to (per-tariff blocks only)

columns.name: value_c_per_day
columns.description: cents per day: per_year x 100 / 365, per_day x 100 ($) ; NULL otherwise

tables.name: tou_schedule
tables.description: A named set of time-of-use windows as stated in one document.
why: Windows are shared by many tariffs and change by year, so they are versioned per document and linked to tariffs through tariff_tou.
time_basis and public-holiday treatment are explicit because distributors differ (local vs standard time; holidays as weekends or not).

columns.name: covers_full_day
columns.description: 1 when the document's windows partition every day (tested: 24h, no overlap)

columns.name: locator
columns.description: Where in the document: xlsx:<sheet>!<cell>, pdf:p<page>, pdf-ocr:p<page> or html:text (grammar in scripts/tariffdb/locators.py)

columns.name: quote
columns.description: Verbatim wording from the document at the locator (whitespace-insensitive match is tested)

tables.name: tou_window
tables.description: One time window: period, day type, start/end time, months.
why: Times are 'HH:MM' with an exclusive end ('24:00' allowed) so windows tile a day without gaps or overlaps; months are explicit so seasonal windows need no special casing.
checks: months IS NOT NULL OR season IS NOT NULL

columns.name: end_time
columns.description: exclusive; 24:00 = midnight at the end of the day

columns.name: months
columns.description: comma-separated month numbers 1-12 the window applies in; NULL when the source names a season without listing its months (exception season_months_not_stated)

columns.name: locator
columns.description: Where in the document: xlsx:<sheet>!<cell>, pdf:p<page>, pdf-ocr:p<page> or html:text (grammar in scripts/tariffdb/locators.py)

columns.name: quote
columns.description: Verbatim wording from the document at the locator (whitespace-insensitive match is tested)

tables.name: tou_window_month
tables.description: Relational month membership of each TOU window.
why: Month joins do not need comma-separated string matching; tou_window.months retains the readable extraction.

tables.name: tariff_tou
tables.description: Which TOU schedule a tariff uses, for which kind of charge, in which year.
why: A tariff can have different windows for energy, demand and export charges.

columns.name: locator
columns.description: Where in the document: xlsx:<sheet>!<cell>, pdf:p<page>, pdf-ocr:p<page> or html:text (grammar in scripts/tariffdb/locators.py)

columns.name: quote
columns.description: Verbatim wording from the document at the locator (whitespace-insensitive match is tested)

tables.name: demand_rule
tables.description: How billed demand is measured: kW or kVA, interval, aggregation, window, months, minimums.
why: Demand prices are meaningless without the measurement rule; the rule is a row so one rule can serve several tariffs and components.

columns.name: interval_minutes
columns.description: metering interval the maximum is taken over

columns.name: aggregation
columns.description: how the billed figure is derived

columns.name: aggregation_count
columns.description: n for average_of_highest_days (e.g. 4 highest days in the month)

columns.name: months
columns.description: months the charge applies; NULL when the rule states none (a linked window carries any season)

columns.name: locator
columns.description: Where in the document: xlsx:<sheet>!<cell>, pdf:p<page>, pdf-ocr:p<page> or html:text (grammar in scripts/tariffdb/locators.py)

columns.name: quote
columns.description: Verbatim wording from the document at the locator (whitespace-insensitive match is tested)

tables.name: tariff_demand_rule
tables.description: Which demand rule a tariff's demand component uses.
why: Peak and off-peak demand components of one tariff can follow different rules.

columns.name: time_band
columns.description: component band it governs (NULL = all demand components)

tables.name: eligibility_rule
tables.description: Requirements and assignment rules: customer type, voltage, consumption/demand thresholds, meter type, default/opt-in/opt-out, closure, required technology.
why: Requirements are heterogeneous, so each is one typed row (rule_type + operator + number + unit) rather than dozens of mostly-empty columns; every rule quotes its source.
checks: value_num IS NOT NULL OR value_text IS NOT NULL OR target_tariff_id IS NOT NULL

columns.name: value_unit
columns.description: unit of the threshold (MWh/yr, kVA, kW, kV ...)

columns.name: value_text
columns.description: categorical value (residential, LV, interval, default, opt_in, ...)

columns.name: target_tariff_id
columns.description: tariff referred to (opt-out target, required companion)

columns.name: locator
columns.description: Where in the document: xlsx:<sheet>!<cell>, pdf:p<page>, pdf-ocr:p<page> or html:text (grammar in scripts/tariffdb/locators.py)

columns.name: quote
columns.description: Verbatim wording from the document at the locator (whitespace-insensitive match is tested)

tables.name: price_adjustment
tables.description: A documented difference between AER and distributor prices for one distributor-year (metering adder, ACT LFiT adder or rebate, rounding artefact).
why: The known AER-vs-distributor offsets are explained by data with a formula and evidence, so a consumer can derive the distributor price from the AER price.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: uniform amount when there is one

columns.name: evidence_document_id
columns.description: document stating or containing the amount

columns.name: locator
columns.description: Where in the document: xlsx:<sheet>!<cell>, pdf:p<page>, pdf-ocr:p<page> or html:text (grammar in scripts/tariffdb/locators.py)

columns.name: quote
columns.description: Verbatim wording from the document at the locator (whitespace-insensitive match is tested)

tables.name: price_adjustment_tariff
tables.description: Tariffs an adjustment applies to, with the expected per-tariff difference.
why: Metering adders differ by tariff (only small-customer tariffs carry them); listing the tariffs makes the rule testable.

tables.name: exception_type
tables.description: Catalogue of irregularities the data must represent, and how it represents each.
why: Exceptions are first-class data with a stated representation and a test, so new years can be checked against the same catalogue.

tables.name: exception_instance
tables.description: Each occurrence of a catalogued exception.
why: Occurrences point at the exact tariff/listing/charge/document affected.

columns.name: distributor_id
columns.description: distributor affected (NULL for multi-distributor AER documents)

columns.name: related_document_id
columns.description: second document (e.g. approved version vs v1)

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: size of the effect where numeric
